knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Planning the crew's day and tracking progress are core leading tasks. Pay decisions, hiring and supplier contracts sit above the team leader.
A team leader usually leads a smaller group, while a manager may oversee several teams. The other options describe decisions that usually sit above the team leader.
Checking the role list and agreeing the boundary with the supervisor protects core work and makes any change visible. Refusing without reason, or dropping crew work silently, are both poor responses.

practicalCriteria: The learner's role description lists core, secondary and other-person tasks in separate headed lists, and a supervisor can match each item to the business's job description.
The learner names at least two decisions that need supervisor approval and states who to refer them to.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Observed or recorded discussion in which a task is declined or referred, with reason
stopWorkCriteria: Stop and refer any request that would make the lead decide pay, discipline or dismissal without a delegation in writing.
Stop and refer any task outside the lead's trained or authorised work.
